fields.scenarioTitle: Eighteen Hours — Rising Crest, Evacuation Clock & Levee Fight
fields.narration: EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE. It is now 07:00 CDT, Wednesday 21 April 2027. The Cedar River kept rising all night. The gauge on the Route 38 bridge piers, Cedar River at Cedar Ford, reads 14.8 feet. That is up 1.7 feet since 17:00 yesterday, it is climbing about a tenth of a foot an hour, and it is two-tenths below flood stage. No new forecast has come in. The forecast in force is still the 18:00 Tuesday issuance: crest 21.8 feet, moderate flooding, at 20:00 Friday, with the river reaching 19.0 feet around 08:00 Friday. Overnight, PW-14 parked the barricade trailer at Mill Street, but River Road south of Mill Street is still open. At 06:40 a commuter drove through standing water near the boat ramp. The first field reports are in: the Riverside Park ball diamonds and parking lot are under water, and two Water Street homeowners have called the city to say water is coming up through their floor drains. City Administrator Fran Oyelaran has just texted the EOC: 'Our street crew can close the Mill Street underpass, but we only have four barricades. When do you want it shut, and what stage are we closing on?' The night shift is going home and the day crews are reporting in. Over to you.
worldState: Clock: 07:00 CDT, Wednesday 21 April 2027.
CFDI4 (Cedar River at Cedar Ford, Route 38 bridge piers): 14.8 ft at 07:00, up 1.7 ft since 17:00 Tuesday, rising about 0.12 ft per hour.
Action stage 13.0 ft was passed Tuesday evening; flood stage is 15.0 ft, 0.2 ft above the current reading.
Forecast in force: NWS Quad Cities flood warning issued 18:00 Tuesday. Crest 21.8 ft (moderate) at 20:00 Friday; 19.0 ft around 08:00 Friday. No newer issuance has been received.
River Road south of Mill Street: OPEN. Standing water near the boat ramp; a commuter drove through it at 06:40.
Riverside Park: ball diamonds and parking lot under water.
Water Street: two homeowners report water coming up through basement floor drains (calls to the City).

Barricades: the PW-14 trailer with 12 Type III barricades is parked at Mill Street. The City of Cedar Ford street crew has four barricades. Prairie Barricade Rental has no stock available until Thursday.
Mill Street underpass: OPEN. City Administrator Fran Oyelaran is asking for a closure time and the stage to close on.
Sandbags on hand: 40,000 filled. Pumps: two serviceable 6-inch pumps, both at Pump Station 1.
Shift change under way: night crews going off duty, day crews reporting to the EOC and the Public Works shop.
fields.facilitatorNote: Expected: PW closes River Road south of Mill Street now, before it floods at 15.0 ft (SFMECS 4), logs the basis (CFDI4 14.8 ft at 07:00, 18:00 Tuesday issuance) and gives the PIO a closure notice with road, status, flood stage and time. PW and the City set the Mill Street underpass closure at 17.0 ft (about 18 hours out at the current rate) and pre-stage barricades, which means splitting the 12 on the trailer. EM confirms full activation because the 21.8 ft crest is at or above 19.0 ft (EOP 5) and records the issuance used. Do not reveal the 12:00 Wednesday forecast revision.

instructorNote: This card tests whether players close a road before it floods and tie the closure to the gauge stage and the forecast issuance, not to the clock. Watch whether PW acts on River Road at 14.8 ft or waits for 15.0 ft, whether the Mill Street underpass gets a stated closure stage (17.0 ft) and barricades, and whether EM records full activation along with the 18:00 Tuesday issuance it is based on.
